ud8.2:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Wood, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
ud8.2:1.3: o Then at that time the Fortunate One was instructing, rousing, enthusing, and cheering the monks with a Dhamma talk connected with Emancipation. Those monks, after making it their goal, applying their minds,
ud8.2:1.4: considering it with all their mind, were listening to Dhamma with an attentive ear.
ud8.2:2.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud8.2:3.2: “What is called ‘the uninclined’ (Emancipation) is hard to see, ~ for it is not easy to see the truth,
ud8.2:3.4: For the one who knows, who has penetrated craving, ~ for the one who sees there is nothing (no defilements).”
